meta.name: Monitor solar generation and grid usage with Open-Meteo data and Slack alerts

parameters.content:
## Solar Energy Generation & Usage Monitor

Daily solar performance and household energy-usage check. Pulls actual solar production, grid/meter usage and a weather forecast, models what the system SHOULD have produced given the day's sunlight, flags under-performance, and — for real problems — walks through a human-in-the-loop acknowledgement/resolution cycle before anything is closed out.

### How it works
1. Runs on a daily schedule (evening, after sunset) or manually for testing
2. Set - Config centralizes the solar API, grid/meter API and weather API URLs, system capacity, performance thresholds, tariff rates and the notify channel
3. Three API calls run in sequence: HTTP Request - Fetch Solar Production Data (today's produced kWh), HTTP Request - Fetch Grid Usage Data (today's consumed kWh), HTTP Request - Fetch Weather Forecast (hourly cloud cover / solar radiation)
4. JS - Compute Expected Solar Output & Efficiency Ratio models expected kWh from the weather data (a simplified irradiance-based capacity-factor model with a performance derate) and compares it to actual production
5. JS - Analyze Usage vs Production & Compute Net Energy Balance matches production and usage by interval to compute self-consumption, grid import/export, peak usage time, and a peak/off-peak-weighted grid-import cost
6. JS - Build Alert/Report Payload & Determine Severity combines both analyses into a severity level (none/warning/critical) with a troubleshooting checklist for real problems
7. If an alert is required, the flow pauses for a human to acknowledge it, then pauses again for confirmation the issue was resolved, escalating at either step if nothing comes back

### How to set up
1. Import this workflow into n8n
2. Add credentials: your solar-monitoring API (SolarEdge/Enphase/etc.) and your utility/smart-meter API on the respective HTTP Request nodes, plus Slack (chat:write) — the weather API (Open-Meteo style) needs no key
3. Edit Set - Config: solarApiUrl, gridUsageApiUrl, weatherApiUrl, latitude/longitude, systemCapacityKw, underperformanceThresholdPercent, criticalThresholdPercent, tariff rates, notifyChannel
4. Point the two Wait nodes' resume webhooks at your alerting UI's 'acknowledge' and 'mark resolved' actions
5. Activate the workflow, or use the Manual Trigger to test end to end

nodes.name: Sticky Note - Trigger, Config & Data Fetch

parameters.content:
## 1. Trigger, Config & Three Data Sources

Set - Config centralizes every knob: API URLs, system capacity, location, performance thresholds, tariff rates and the notify channel.

Three HTTP Request nodes each pull one data source: HTTP Request - Fetch Solar Production Data (today's produced kWh, interval by interval), HTTP Request - Fetch Grid Usage Data (today's consumed kWh, interval by interval), HTTP Request - Fetch Weather Forecast (hourly cloud cover and shortwave radiation for the day). All three feed the analysis stage that follows.

## 2. Three Advanced Analysis Steps

JS - Compute Expected Solar Output & Efficiency Ratio integrates hourly radiation and cloud-cover data into an expected-kWh estimate (capacity factor vs. STC-normalized radiation, discounted for cloud cover and a fixed performance derate), then compares it to actual production and flags a hard zero-production-during-daylight fault.

JS - Analyze Usage vs Production & Compute Net Energy Balance matches production and usage by timestamp to compute self-consumption, grid import/export totals, the peak usage interval, and a peak/off-peak tariff-weighted grid-import cost.

JS - Build Alert/Report Payload & Determine Severity combines both into a severity level (none/warning/critical), a plain-English report message, and a troubleshooting checklist for real faults.

## 3. Alert Acknowledgement, Resolution & Delivery

IF - Alert Required routes: no alert -> straight to Slack - Send Daily Summary. Alert -> Wait - For Alert Acknowledgement pauses until someone acknowledges it; IF - Acknowledged gates a second pause, Wait - For Resolution Confirmation, before IF - Resolved decides between Slack - Send Resolution Confirmed and Slack - Escalate Unresolved Issue. An unacknowledged alert escalates on its own via Slack - Escalate Unacknowledged Alert. Every Slack node uses continueOnFail so a delivery hiccup doesn't fail the run.
